title: CPR
subtitle: Adult
summary: Hands-only CPR for an adult. The 2025 guidelines direct telecommunicators to coach Hands-Only CPR for adults and conventional CPR with breaths for children, which is why this protocol branches by age at entry.

steps.speech: First. Is it safe where you are?

steps.detail: You cannot help anyone if you are hurt. Move to safety, then call 911.
steps.speech: Get yourself clear first. You cannot help if you are hurt. Then call nine one one.

steps.detail: Tap both shoulders hard. Shout their name.
steps.speech: Tap both shoulders. Shout at them. Do they move?

steps.detail: They are responding, so do not start compressions. Call 911 and keep watching their breathing.
steps.speech: They are responding. Do not start compressions. Call nine one one and stay with them.

steps.detail: Say: "YOU — call 911." Then point at another person: "YOU — find an AED."
steps.speech: Point at one person. Say: you, call nine one one. Point at another. Say: you, find an A E D.

steps.detail: Speaker on. Phone down beside you. I will keep the beat on screen.
steps.speech: Call nine one one. Speaker on. Put the phone down beside you.

steps.detail: Watch the chest for 10 seconds. Gasping is NOT breathing.
steps.speech: Watch their chest for ten seconds. Gasping is not breathing.
steps.quote: The No-No-Go framework is reiterated as an effective method for recognizing OHCA.

steps.detail: Keep watching. If the breathing stops or turns to gasping, come back and start compressions.
steps.speech: Roll them onto their side. Keep watching. If breathing stops, come straight back.

steps.detail: On the floor, not a bed. Kneel so their chest is about level with your knees.
steps.speech: Get them flat on the floor. Not a bed. Kneel beside them.
steps.quote: For adult cardiac arrest, rescuers should perform chest compressions with the patient on a firm surface and with the patient's torso at approximately the level of the rescuer's knees.

steps.detail: Heel of one hand on the centre of the chest. Other hand on top. Lock your elbows.
steps.speech: Heel of one hand on the centre of the chest. Other hand on top. Lock your elbows.
steps.quote: Hand placement on the lower half of the sternum for adult chest compressions.

steps.detail: Hard and fast. Let the chest come all the way up between pushes.
steps.speech: Push hard and fast. Follow the beat. Let the chest come all the way back up.
steps.depthCoaching: Push down about two inches. Let it come all the way up.
steps.quote: Chest compressions at a rate of 100 to 120 per minute to a depth of at least 2 inches (5 cm) but not greater than 2.4 inches (6 cm) for an average adult, allowing full chest recoil.
steps.verificationNote: Rate and depth are carried forward from the 2020 Guidelines and are NOT listed among the 2025 changes, which is good evidence they are unchanged — but ahajournals.org and cpr.heart.org both return 403 to automated fetches, so this could not be confirmed against the primary PDF. Confirm manually before real-world use.

steps.detail: Do not stop compressions to go looking. Only stop if someone hands you one.
steps.speech: Has anyone brought an A E D?

steps.detail: The AED talks you through it. Bare the chest — you can move a bra aside, you do not have to remove it.
steps.speech: Turn it on and do what it says. Bare the chest. You can move a bra aside. You do not have to take it off.
steps.quote: When placing pads for defibrillation for an adult in cardiac arrest, it might be reasonable to adjust the position of a bra instead of removing it.

steps.detail: The moment the shock is delivered — or if it says no shock — go straight back to pushing.
steps.speech: As soon as it has shocked, go straight back to pushing. Do not wait.
